linkedin.title: I started building a news app when I was a teenager because I was tired of missing the stories that actually mattered to me.
linkedin.body:
It felt like a paradox. We live in an era of infinite information, yet finding quality news that fits my specific interests felt like digging for gold in a landfill. The algorithms I encountered were designed to keep me clicking, not to keep me informed.

I realized that the problem wasn't a lack of news. It was a lack of curation. I wanted a way to filter out the noise and focus on the topics that shaped my world without having to check twenty different sources every morning.

That frustration became the foundation for Headlinne. We wanted to build something different. Instead of chasing engagement metrics, we focused on using AI to understand what a reader truly cares about and delivering that directly to them. It is about respecting the reader's time and intelligence.

Building this as a teenager taught me that you do not need decades of industry experience to see when a system is broken. Sometimes, you just need to be a curious user who wants a better way to stay informed.
linkedin.cta: If you are tired of the noise, you can see how we are rethinking the news experience at HEADLINNE.com.

story_card.caption:
A new study shows electric vehicle batteries retain 90 percent of their capacity after 150,000 kilometers.
